summary.name: Software project management (Wikipedia)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing software project management: the planning and leading of software projects, common failure causes, and key processes such as risk, requirements, change, and release management.
keywords: how to manage a software project
use_cases: reviewing risk and requirements management practices
studying bug and issue severity levels
background reading for a software project manager
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It defines software project management as a sub-discipline of project management and lists common causes of software project failure, such as poor communication, unrealistic goals, and badly defined requirements. It describes development process areas including risk, requirements, change, configuration, and release management, and covers project planning, monitoring, and control. It also explains issue severity levels (critical to trivial) and issue management.
notable: Lists the most common causes of software project failure
Explains the shift from the waterfall model toward cyclic delivery
Defines issue severity levels from critical to trivial
Cites sources including IEEE and ISO standards and books on software project management
caveats: Describes concepts and methods, not a specific software tool
Some sections are flagged by Wikipedia as possibly containing original research and having multiple issues
